title: What Is Next.js?
summary: Understand what Next.js is—a full-stack React framework—why it exists, and how the App Router renders components on the server by default.

title: Creating a Next.js App
summary: Scaffold a new project with create-next-app, tour the files it generates, and run the development server to see live changes.

title: Pages and File-Based Routing
summary: Learn how folders and page.tsx files in the app/ directory map directly to your application's URLs, including nested routes.

title: Layouts and Nested Layouts
summary: Use layout.tsx to share UI like navigation across pages, and nest layouts so each section of your app can add its own wrapper.

title: Linking and Navigation
summary: Move between routes with the Link component for fast client-side navigation, and navigate programmatically with the useRouter hook.

title: Server and Client Components
summary: Understand the App Router's biggest idea: components render on the server by default, and you opt into the browser with the 'use client' directive.

title: Styling Your App
summary: Compare Next.js's built-in styling options—global CSS, CSS Modules, Tailwind, and inline styles—and know when to reach for each.

title: Images, Fonts, and Static Assets
summary: Use next/image and next/font to serve optimized images and self-hosted fonts, and learn how the public/ folder serves static files.

title: Dynamic Routes and Route Params
summary: Create routes with dynamic segments like [id], read the (async) params in Next.js 15, and pre-render them with generateStaticParams.

title: Fetching Data in Server Components
summary: Fetch data directly inside async Server Components with await—no useEffect—and avoid waterfalls by loading independent data in parallel.

title: Rendering Strategies: Static and Dynamic
summary: Learn how Next.js chooses between static rendering (at build time) and dynamic rendering (per request), and how to control it.

title: Caching and Revalidation
summary: Control data freshness with fetch caching options and revalidation—time-based (ISR) and on-demand with revalidatePath and revalidateTag.

title: Loading UI and Streaming
summary: Show instant loading states with loading.tsx and stream slow parts of a page independently using React Suspense boundaries.

title: Error Handling
summary: Catch runtime errors per route with error.tsx (a Client Component with reset), and show 404s with not-found.tsx and the notFound() function.

title: Route Handlers and APIs
summary: Build API endpoints inside your app with route.ts files that export HTTP method handlers and return Response objects.

title: Metadata and SEO
summary: Set page titles, descriptions, and social-share tags with the Metadata API—static via the metadata export and dynamic via generateMetadata.

title: Server Actions and Mutations
summary: Run server-side mutations directly from your components with Server Actions—async functions marked 'use server' that handle forms and refresh data.

title: Forms, useActionState, and Optimistic UI
summary: Add rich form UX to Server Actions with React 19 hooks: useActionState for results and errors, useFormStatus for pending state, and useOptimistic for instant feedback.

title: Middleware
summary: Run code before a request is completed with middleware.ts—redirect, rewrite, or add headers—and scope it to specific paths with a matcher.

title: Parallel and Intercepting Routes
summary: Render multiple pages in one layout with parallel routes (@slots), and load a route in the current context with intercepting routes—the classic modal pattern.

title: Authentication Patterns
summary: Understand authentication vs authorization, session strategies with secure cookies, and where to enforce access checks in the App Router.

title: The Caching Model in Depth
summary: Understand Next.js's four caching layers—Request Memoization, Data Cache, Full Route Cache, and the client Router Cache—and how each is invalidated.

title: Performance and Optimization
summary: Ship less JavaScript and improve Core Web Vitals with Server Components, dynamic imports, image/font optimization, and next/script.

title: Deploying to Production
summary: Ship a Next.js app: compare Vercel, Node self-hosting, and static export, handle environment variables, and know each target's trade-offs.
